title: Pin rule markers, index rows and spoken lines with one text-reading test
action:
Add packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/tests/rule_index_parity.rs, per pstack-gaps D6. Copy the shape of tests/route_class_parity.rs and tests/specs_fence.rs: a pure filesystem test that READS the repo's files as text. Import nothing from the bee crate — ROUTE_CLASS_VALUES-style constants are module-private and re-declaring a list in a test reproduces the close.rs duplication trap this feature exists to avoid.

The test walks up from CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR to the repo root the same way its siblings do, then asserts THREE things:

1. The set of rule ids in `<!-- rule: <id> -->` markers in AGENTS.md equals the set in packages/bee/AGENTS.block.md. A mismatch fails naming every id present in one file and missing from the other, in both directions.
2. That set equals the set of rule rows in the `## AGENTS.md rule homes` section of docs/knowledge/areas/doctrine-layer/router-triage-and-the-agents-md-duplication-boundary.md. A row is a line matching ``- `<id>` (``. The failure names the unindexed markers and the indexed-but-unmarked rows separately.
3. Every row in that section carries a non-empty `spoken:` line before its `applied_at:` line. The failure names each rule id whose spoken line is missing or blank.

Parse the section by finding the exact heading `## AGENTS.md rule homes` and stopping at the next `\n## ` — the same boundary parse_agents_rule_homes uses in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/knowledge/ownership.rs — so the test and the parser cannot disagree about where the section ends. Every failure message names the file and the offending id, never just a count.

RED-FIRST PROOF, required: after the test compiles green, delete ONE `spoken:` line from the index file, run `cargo test --test rule_index_parity` and record that it FAILS naming that rule id, then restore the line and record the green run. Both outputs go in the cap's verification evidence. A test that was never seen red proves only that it compiles.

Do not modify any file other than the new test.
verify: `PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --test rule_index_parity` is green, AND the recorded red run (one spoken line removed) failed naming that rule id. Both command outputs are in the cap evidence.

truths: packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/tests/rule_index_parity.rs exists, imports nothing from the bee crate, and reads AGENTS.md, packages/bee/AGENTS.block.md and the index file as text.
The test asserts marker-set equality between AGENTS.md and AGENTS.block.md, equality of that set with the index rows, and a non-empty spoken line on every row.
Every failure message names the file and the offending rule id, never only a count.
The section boundary is found by the exact heading `## AGENTS.md rule homes` and the next `\n## `, matching parse_agents_rule_homes.
The test was seen RED: one spoken line removed made it fail naming that rule id, and the restored file made it green; both outputs are in the cap evidence.
